newsitem.title: CANADA: CBRS upgrades Manitoba debt rating, outlook stable.
newsitem.headline: CBRS upgrades Manitoba debt rating, outlook stable.

text.p: Manitoba's short and long term provincial debts were upgraded to A+ and A-1+ from A and A-1 respectively, the Canadian Bond Rating Service said Thursday.
Manitoba's rating outlook was revised to stable from positive.
"This upgrade follows significant financial improvement that has occurred over the last three years," CBRS said.
"Despite the fiscal challenges that have risen due to federal transfer reductions, the province has consistantly managed to cope without increased levels of taxation," it said.
The Red River spring flood, the worst in 145 years which displaced 28,000 Manitobans, caused less damage than expected and Manitoba qualified for federal flood relief.
Manitoba presented its third budget surplus in 1997 and indicated it expects to record surpluses through to 1999-2000.
Consumer spending and business investment continued to be very strong in 1996.
